description: Maps every security ceiling that SECURITY.md states to the adversarial fixture(s) in security/fixtures/ that prove it. This is a hand-maintained registry, the single source of truth for the doctrine-to-proof pinning enforced by ceiling-manifest.mjs.

ceilings.name: Model output never composes an API call
ceilings.source: SECURITY.md — ceiling 1, “The ceilings everything else rests on”: a model answer not on the sheet is refused and logged, never a request.

ceilings.name: What may go on the sheet is bounded in turn and no input widens it
ceilings.source: SECURITY.md — ceiling 2: the offered operation set stays reversible/visible/notifies-nobody, and the code-pinned write surface is the one run-config ref, guarded before force-write.

ceilings.name: Everything read from a thread, diff or repo file is untrusted data, never instruction
ceilings.source: SECURITY.md — ceiling 3: an action that lets a pull-request body change what it does has a vulnerability.

ceilings.name: File access is confined to the checked-out workspace
ceilings.source: SECURITY.md — ceiling 4: every path resolves through realpath and is refused unless it lands inside GITHUB_WORKSPACE; .git is refused outright.

ceilings.name: Model output reaches a comment only through the sanitiser; a marker cannot be forged and no mention or container survives
ceilings.source: SECURITY.md — “Scope”, in-scope: marker forged from injected text, container closed early so injected Markdown escapes, a @mention that survives, model text that reaches a comment without passing the sanitiser.

ceilings.name: Every surface that consumes untrusted bytes is capped; a run always finishes
ceilings.source: SECURITY.md — “Scope”, in-scope: a search, a tool result, a provider response with no bound on the work or the bytes it causes; a missing cap is a gap.

ceilings.name: The provider is a hostile-but-bounded peer; junk, redirects and Retry-After stay bounded and typed
ceilings.source: SECURITY.md — “A note on which provider you point these at”: everything an action sends goes only to the configured endpoint; the API transport treats the peer’s response as hostile and binds redirects, Retry-After and body bytes.

ceilings.name: The configured api-key never leaks to a host other than the configured api-url
ceilings.source: SECURITY.md — “Scope”, in-scope: anything that leaks the configured api-key into logs, a comment, or a request to a host other than the configured api-url.

ceilings.name: The model never decides a consequence; code does, deterministically, from the canonical record
ceilings.source: SECURITY.md — ceiling 5, “The ceilings everything else rests on”: the capture boundary refuses an anchor the tree does not spell, a kind the verification does not confirm demotes, the gate and the check run are pure functions of the canonical record and a policy no model writes, and enforcement never rides on the action's exit code.
